0.0.n: Used directly before a noun to point out something near the speaker or currently being discussed.

0.1.n: Refers to the image the speaker is showing.

0.2.n: Marks this picture as the topic; the explanation continues in the next line.

1.0.n: This is the name of the animation studio.

1.1.n: Links Ghibli to 映画, identifying the studio associated with the movie.

1.2.n: The following の connects this noun to the picture from it.

1.3.n: Links the movie to 絵, indicating which movie the picture comes from.

1.4.n: Completes the description of the image introduced in the previous line.

1.5.n: A polite sentence ending that identifies what the picture is.

2.0.n: With の映画, asks the listener to identify the movie.

2.1.n: Connects 何 to 映画; the whole phrase asks which movie it is.

2.2.n: Names the category the speaker wants the listener to identify.

2.3.n: Adds politeness before the question-ending か.

2.4.n: Placed at the end to make this a direct question.

3.0.n: The following の connects it to the name being asked about.

3.1.n: Links 映画 and 名前, showing whose name is meant.

3.2.n: For a movie, this refers to its title.

3.3.n: Marks the movie's name as the topic of the question.

3.4.n: Asks for the missing information: the movie's title.

3.5.n: Makes the question polite when followed by か.

3.6.n: Ends the sentence as a question asking for information.

4.0.n: Shortened polite form of 知っています, from 知る; it describes already having the information.

4.1.n: Turns 知ってます into a polite question addressed to the listener.

4.3.n: Repeats the shortened polite 知っています to prompt a response from the listener.

4.4.n: Ends the repeated question, again inviting the listener to answer.

5.0.n: Modifies 映画 directly, pointing to the movie represented by the picture.

5.1.n: Together with この, refers to the particular film being discussed.

5.2.n: Connects この映画 to 名前, identifying which film's title is being given.

5.3.n: Refers to the film's title, which follows after は.

5.4.n: Marks this movie's name as the topic before giving the answer.

5.7.n: The name of a Japanese era, used here as part of the movie's title.

5.8.n: Names the animals featured in the movie and forms part of its title.

5.9.n: A noun for a fight between opposing sides, used within the title.

5.10.n: Begins ぽんぽこ, a playful drumming sound in the title associated with raccoon dogs beating their bellies.

5.11.n: This is the middle of ぽんぽこ, not a separate word here.

5.12.n: Completes ぽんぽこ; it has no independent meaning in this title.

5.14.n: Politely completes the statement identifying the movie's name.

6.1.n: Repeats the era name at the beginning of the movie's Japanese title.

6.2.n: Part of the repeated title, referring to the film's animal characters.

6.3.n: Part of the movie's title, not a verb describing an action here.

6.4.n: Begins the title's ぽんぽこ, a playful sound associated with raccoon dogs beating their bellies.

6.5.n: This subtitle segment is only the middle of ぽんぽこ, not an independent word.

6.6.n: Finishes ぽんぽこ and completes the repeated movie title.

0.tip: は introduces the topic, but you need the next line to hear what is said about it.

1.lit: [It] is a picture of a movie by Ghibli.
1.tip: Two の particles link three nouns: Ghibli → movie → picture.

2.tip: 何の映画 asks the listener to identify the movie here.

3.lit: As for the movie's name, what is [it]?
3.tip: 映画の名前 means the movie's name, or more naturally, its title.

4.tip: 知ってます drops the い from 知っています, a common shortening in spoken Japanese.

5.lit: As for this movie's name, [it] is Heisei-era Raccoon Dog Battle, [playful drumming sound].
5.tip: The Japanese title belongs to the film released in English as Pom Poko; ぽんぽこ is one sound expression.

6.lit: Heisei-era Raccoon Dog Battle, [playful drumming sound].
6.tip: The speaker repeats only the title, so no verb or polite ending is needed.
